title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: External stimuli switch rare-earth molecular materials by coordination-bond rearrangement, supramolecular reorganization, electronic rearrangement, or structural relaxation, and orthogonal stimuli can address different channels in one assembly.
explanation: The section frames photo-, electro-, and magneto-responsive groups as giving reversible luminescence or magnetic-relaxation switching. Eu nanoparticles respond orthogonally to pH, temperature, and light through coordination dissociation, nonradiative decay, and photochemical ring opening/closing. An Eu-MOF heterostructure first aggregates tetracarboxylate ligands under solvent to give AIE, then changes ligand dihedral angle under LED light for a second color and intensity change.
scope: Stimuli-responsive lanthanide nanoparticles and Eu-MOF heterostructures for dynamic luminescence.
conditions: Changes in pH, temperature, or illumination for Eu-NPs; sequential solvent then LED stimulation for the SSR Eu-MOF.
caveats: Orthogonality is demonstrated for the cited Eu-NP system, not asserted for every multistimulus lanthanide material.
